_help.about: Roads (design 30 Sept §BC): a trail network laid before plants, built by whoever left the ruins and maintained by nobody. Links ruins, camps, springs, fords and passes; follows rivers and contours; rivers are the other road type. Restart after editing.
_help.network: Node kinds the roads connect, the least spacing between nodes, the longest single link, and grade limits (roads switchback above max_grade).
_help.trail: Width band; the ground material; wear 0-1 (how bare the tread is); overgrown 0-1 (how much the understory has taken it back); understory kept clear this far either side; a tree planted within tree_at_bend_m of each bend (§AG 7).
_help.decay: Share of bridges that are out (both abutments always stand); share of trails that end at a collapse; waymark spacing, the share fallen, and their kinds. Added 1 Oct (§BY): notched_tree and stone_step as waymark kinds.
_help.landmarks: Off-road finds: how far off the trail (must be out of sight of it), and what kinds.
_help.forks: A fork must be readable this far before it: you can see the other road across the gorge. One-way gates a fork can commit you through.
_help.desire_lines: Design 30 Sept night §BY (pushed 1 Oct): the LIVE road layer. Every folk trip (camps.json sim.jobs) and every pass of the player stamps wear_per_pass on the ground along a width_m strip; it shows once wear passes show_at_wear (grass thins, dirt through) and fades by fade_per_game_day when the walking stops. Paths appear where people actually walk; a camp's gather trails are the first sign it is alive.
_help.lost_and_found: Design 30 Sept night §BY: the old roads are half-forgotten and LONG (Mike). A share of each road (vanish_share) is stretches vanish_len_m long where the trail all but disappears under the understory (overgrown_in_vanish), between clear stretches clear_len_m long; the pickup is marked by a tell within tell_within_m of where the trail resumes (pickup_tells). Losing and refinding the path is the ambient game.
_help.opening_road: Design 30 Sept night §BX (pushed 1 Oct), amended by §CY (3 Oct): the first road. spawn_beside_road: the opening camp sits on the road, never in trackless woods. first_landmark camp_at_ruin: the road leads to a camp restoring a ruin, its hearth glow the beacon. The clock and the road's length are dawn_start's (below); §BX's afternoon keys (spawn.real_min_before_dusk, walk_real_min, walk_speed_mps, detour_allowance_min, arrive_by, length_km_hint) were retired by Claude Code when it wired dawn_start, 3 Oct. Only the opening road is tuned; the rest is network/trail/decay above.
_help.opening_road_dawn_start: The opening at dawn (Mike, 3 Oct: "move to dawn and you'll reach another landmark by dusk ... or before dusk, but hopefully dusk at the latest"). opening_road.dawn_start supersedes the afternoon clock and the half-hour length above; the old afternoon keys are retired (Claude Code, 3 Oct, when this was wired: main.open_clock and World.opening_walk_target read it). spawn.phase dawn, real_min_after_dawn_begins: the clock starts this many real minutes after dawn begins at the spawn's latitude and date (the world still blue, the fire the one warm thing). walk_real_min: the road to the first landmark is this many minutes of straight walking, about half of the daylight you wake with. measure walking_minutes: the road is measured in minutes at the pace the player really walks it (§CR.5's slope pace, built 3 Oct), not in flat kilometres; the first camp is the one whose road to a camp at a ruin comes nearest walk_real_min. length_km_hint is the same walk on dead-flat ground (walk_real_min x 60 x walk_speed_mps, the ambient walk of movement.json), the most the road can be; pace_share_typical is the share of the flat speed ordinary land gives (0.82, pace_check, 3 Oct), so a typical opening road is about 8.5 km. arrive before_dusk, latest dusk_end: a straight walk arrives in the working day; a walk that spends as long looking as walking arrives as dusk begins; dusk itself (18 real min at the reference) is the grace, with the hearth glow ahead. slack_before_dusk_min: a straight walk must arrive at least this long before dusk begins at the spawn's latitude and date; where the day is too short for that, the road is shortened to fit (never the clock moved). first_landmark stays camp_at_ruin (§BX). Checked by tools/fire_circle_check.py against sky/day_cycle.json and tools/reference/daylight_reference.py. First guesses; the designer owns them.
_help.grades_holders_holloway_approach: Design 3 Oct §DM (Mike, from play): the road never leads where you can't follow (network.hard_max_grade is a HARD cap; max_grade stays the soft switchback cost); it widens toward what it leads to (grades, by distance along the link to the nearer node); where it climbs above max_grade it is sunk into the slope (holloway); its line is held by cairns at every bend and pickup, milestones, and a planted avenue on the kerbed approach (holders); the last stretch into a ruin or shrine runs straight at it down the avenue (approach). Built by Claude Code, 5 Oct: grades (RoadNetwork._grades, grade_at: the tread's width, wear and overgrowth blend from kerbed at a ruin, camp or waypoint, to track, to trodden beyond beyond_m; vanishings only on trodden), kerb stones on the kerbed run (RoadProps._kerb), holloways (link.hollow, ground_on sinks the tread), holders (a cairn at every bend, a tell at both ends of every vanishing, a milestone per mile with a notch per mile from the node, the avenue: VegetationPlacer._place_avenue). Not built yet: holloway.bank_roots and bend_trees_lean_in, and approach (§DM.5).

steep_passes._help: Mike, 5 Oct ("allow steeper passes if it makes sense for that environment"; added by Claude Code): high ground lets a road climb steeper than hard_max_grade, as mountain paths do. The cap rises smoothly from hard_max_grade at from_m (the ground's height in the game, metres) to hard_max_grade here at full_m and above; max_grade (the switchback cost) rises in the same proportion. 0.45 is about 24 degrees, still well under walk_max_deg 45 and walked at Tobler's pace (§CR.5). Built: RoadNetwork.hard_max_at, soft_max_at; road_check judges each step against the cap where it stands.

spawn._help_sun_deg: Design 4 Oct §EB.1 (added by Claude Code, 5 Oct): the wake waits until the sun is this high (degrees, below the horizon) at the camp, as well as real_min_after_dawn_begins. One real minute after dawn begins the sun is about 8 degrees down, and the grade reads anything below -6 as full night (SkySystem daylight), so the game woke looking like night. At -3 the sky is the blue before sunrise and the fire still the one warm thing.

grades._help_wider: Mike, 5 Oct ("make the roads a bit wider because they can be easy to lose"; changed by Claude Code): every grade about 0.8 m wider than §DM.2's first guesses (trodden 0.8-1.4 -> 1.4-2.0, track 1.6-2.6 -> 2.4-3.4, kerbed 2.6-3.6 -> 3.4-4.4), the trodden a little more worn and less grown over. Built: RoadNetwork._grades, grade_at.
